title: S&P Global Flash France PMI (Sep 2026) — 07:15 UTC / 03:15 ET, the first print of the European flash morning and the second-largest component of the aggregate
source: EST: two primaries, both fetched direct 2026-09-09 by the sp-global-flash-eurozone-pmi-2026-09-23 initial research. (1) S&P Global's forward PMI calendar, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en (HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes): 'September 23 ... 07:15 UTC S&P Global Flash France PMI'. (2) The publisher's own past-release archive, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/PressReleases?language=en (HTTP 200, 92,883 bytes), shows the same slot actually delivered one month earlier: 'August 21 2026 07:15 UTC | S&P Global Flash France PMI'. 07:15 UTC is 03:15 ET under EDT. Filed estimate on the standing schema gap market-events-data.ts carries — no confirmed-source prefix covers a private PMI compiler — and because this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of sp-global-flash-eurozone-pmi-2026-09-23, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED AS THE OTHER HALF OF THE PRE-ANNOUNCEMENT PAIR, and as the earliest European print of the morning. The proposing ledger's structural finding needs both components on the calendar to be checkable: the publisher's own methodology, quoted verbatim from its August release PDF, is that 'Eurozone manufacturing and services indices are calculated by weighting together the national indices' on Eurostat value-added weights, and France prints 45 minutes before the aggregate it feeds while Germany prints 30 minutes before. By 07:30 UTC the two largest national panels are public; the 08:00 UTC Eurozone headline is therefore materially less new than its name suggests. It is also the marker for when the European risk-tone clock actually starts on this date — 07:15 UTC / 03:15 ET, not 08:00. NOT MEASURED: no first-hand bar work was done on the French print specifically, and the aggregate-level measurement it inherits found no distinguishable US-hours footprint for the European block at all (euro-minus-SPY residual above its own median in 4 of 15 instrument-days at the US open, against a 50% base rate, across three flash days). Filed low on that evidence. See the sibling proposal sp-global-flash-germany-pmi-2026-09-23.from-… for what was deliberately NOT proposed and why. Cheap, dated, self-adjudicating falsifier: the release either lands 2026-09-23 at 07:15 UTC or it does not, settling in 14 days. Nothing here is a trade; estimate widens caution and licenses nothing
